## Checklist

- [ ] PR title is a Conventional Commit (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, ...)

- [ ] **Release note.** If this PR has more than one commit and changes public API,
      its CHANGELOG entry is written into the squash commit body — or it will be
      merged **without** squashing.

<!--
Why that last box exists, since it has caught us twice.

release-please renders only the SUBJECT LINE of the commit that lands on main. A
squash merge collapses every commit body into one commit whose subject is the PR
title, so all of those bodies survive in `git log` and none of them reach the
CHANGELOG or the GitHub release notes. v0.5.0 and v0.6.0 both shipped one-line
entries this way, losing the API list, the memory tables and the measured
benchmarks their specs required.

The GitHub release notes are generated once and are NOT regenerated by a later
docs commit, so fixing this after the fact means editing two artifacts by hand.

Two ways to get it right, either is fine:
  1. Merge without squashing, so each commit body becomes its own entry; or
  2. Paste the release note into the squash commit's body in the merge dialog.

A single-commit PR needs neither: its body already is the squash body.

Related trap, same family: a commit body line beginning with an identifier
followed by `(` silently drops the whole commit from the changelog, and a subject
that is not a Conventional Commit type is invisible to release-please entirely.
-->
